To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

low dose oral enxoximone, when administered in combination with beta blockers and background therapy to patients with advanced HF did not improve major clinical outcomes but may have improved exercise capacity.
the positive inotropist enoximone did not improve major clinical outcomes, including all cause mortality, or exercise capacity in advanced HF.

in the ESSENTIAL programme, low doses of the inotrope agent enoximone did not improve clinical outcomes in patients hospitalized for advanced HF, but did improve exercise capacity as measured by the 6 min walking test, in one of the two identical, randomized controlled trials.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods for the treatment of heart failure.
the development of novel materials and their use in applications in which the materials are used in their pure form or as composites.

the development of novel methods and techniques for solving problems in the field of mathematical modeling of the behavior and properties of various systems and processes, including biological, ecological, physical, technical, and economic ones.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
enoximone is not a treatment option for the patients included in this trial.
the results from the ESSENTIAL trials do not support the use of enoximone in advanced HF.
the ESSENTIAL programme failed to show a beneficial effect of low dose oral inotropic therapy in patients with advanced symptomatic HF.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ESSENTIAL trials did not show any evidence of benefit with the use of enoximone in patients with advanced chronic HF, and the use of enalapril was an important factor in the results.
low dose oral eneximone does not improve major clinical outcomes, but it does improve exercise capacity, at least in some patients with advanced HF.

low dose oral enxomime administration did not improve the composite of mortality or hospitalization for worsening HF, or the 6 min walking test distance, but did improve symptoms, as assessed by PGA, and exercise capacity, as assessed by 6MWTD, in patients with advanced chronic HF who were also receiving guideline recommended background therapy including beta blockers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ESSENTIAL trials provide the first randomized evidence of the lack of benefit of a positive inotroptic agent in HF patients treated with beta blockers.
, despite the fact that the ESSENTIAL trials were not powered for clinical outcomes, they do not provide evidence for the benefit of enoximone.
, despite the use of a novel trial design, with two co primary endpoints, we were unable to detect a significant difference in the primary outcome.
